I don't know - my feeling is it's not ideal but it's probably fine.  If you look at the 1x1 and 0p5x1 you can see the ground through holes are generally close to both a mezzanine ground pin and a ground pad, providing a bunch of really good connections.
The 1x0p5 is a lot worse though - I'll definitely be improving that one.

The flip side of course is that putting holes in this region is also not ideal but probably fine - so I'll leave it to you and the others on this thread!

messages.content: Looks like a different manufacturer to me

Interestingly Claude said:

On price, the LXW part costs about $0.11 in volume, while the HCTL is about $0.36. The genuine Hirose DF40C-60DP-0.4V(51) is only about $0.38 on LCSC with around 15.8k in stock. So the HCTL clone saves you almost nothing over the real Hirose part.

I'd be hesitant to go for a much cheaper connector without getting some, doing a test batch and inspecting. Seems as though cheaper connectors often have a thinner gold plating but not sure how much of an issue this is
@stuart - Maybe we can try some of the cheaper connectors on the designs people are getting free silicon?

We can do but keep in mind while using cheaper connectors is easy, changing the board from 70 to 60 pin is some work: board redesign, adaptor for testing, fw for testing, probably other things too.

Interested to hear others' opinions about this too

Well AIUI everyone with a quarter slot on run 2 is free silicon, so doing something a bit experimental with it is presumably ok.

One issue with quarter slot on run 3 is the price of the CoB is almost as much as the silicon, so if that could actually be reduced in some way that would be a good thing.

My understanding the way testing is setup is it would just be a different carrier board in the test board, and due to the low number of mating cycles, that board is consumable anyway. (As an aside, if the Hirose part has more mating cycles then for the other boards you might save money using that!)

On the other hand, it would introduce complexity and possible confusion, e.g. we’d need different example breakouts and people would need to pick the right one. I could see the quarter slot being different ending up as annoying and it also being slightly unreliable due to the cheap part.

Overall if I were you I would probably not want to do it, just to keep things simple, but it depends how much trying to reduce the cost is a factor.

Also to consider that people may be doing multiple mating cycles after receiving the breakouts boards too. I feel like it would be a shame to ship lower quality boards with lower reliable mating connections for the sake of ~20 cents a board

1. As one of the 3 people that has already spent 1.5k USD for getting the run 3 quarter slot assembled** I care about YIELD ! **

The quarter slot assembly cost is the same as all the 1x1 even though there are 18 less wires, making it already the less expensive one to assemble. If this is a question of costs there are other cost factors that do not have any impact on yield that I think should be questioned first: like the decision to go to 4 layers rather than staying on the current 2.

2. As the person making the change, I originally signed up to make some last minute changes and fell blind sighted by this request so late in the development cycle, and so, unlike with my previous change I will not be sending this board for fabrication at my expense to validate it with JLC. Also if I do make the change I will not be maintaining 2 quarter slot versions with the different connector as that is more work that I originally signed up for. I believe other people may also share this felling but might be politer than me and not put it as bluntly.
Yeap! We would need someone to design the boards, the testing setup carrier and such.

FWIW - We have been using the free designs (that people didn't want more off) on Run #1 to work through the CoB yield issues. People who paid on Run #1 should be getting back the full amount of parts. Run #1 was also a single lot run (and the first time we did things), which made the number of die coming back a bit tighter than I would have liked.

There should also plenty of spare die on Run #2 (compared to Run #1) so even if we had a low yield rate means you should be getting back 1,000 mounted parts.
@Essen - We also only had one quarter slot design on Run #1 -- so limited number of parts to work with, so it also got left till last.

We also have 9 quarter slots on Run #2 (all of which were provided for free by me), so will have plenty of silicon to test and make sure the bonding for quarter slots is working correctly and make sure that Run #3 people who paid for stuff get back something that is awesome.
At the moment, it is unclear if there would be a cost reduction by reducing the number of bonds by ~20%

My long term goal is for wafer.space to ***not*** be involved with the CoB mounting side of things but still support ordering with your silicon type set up - kinda like getting a stencil from OHS Park.
I'll probably be able to do that when we finally get people like NextPCB to accept CoB as part of PCBA.
The only reason I'm doing wire bonding right now is that I refuse to let my customers pay >$10 USD per die to get things packaged -- which is the *cheapest* quote I got from other groups.
It would sure suck to pay $2 USD for your silicon and then $10 USD for packaging 😛
As of right now, I'm not 100% sure we have gotten to the point of me ***not*** losing money on the $1.50 USD packaging.

@Essen - I'm also trying to figure out a way to let people "share" slots while still allowing CoB bonding so that we can do things like put two quarter slots in a single half slot or four quarter slots into a 1x1
